item.title: ‘Three of my supporters were killed’ – LG chair reacts to Omo-Agege’s assassination claim
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi, Ochuko Akuopha, Akpokona Omafuaire & Efe Onodjae UGHELLI – Olorogun Jaro Egbo, the local government chairman of Ughelli North, Delta State, were Senator Ovie Omo-Agege said an assassination attempt was made on his life, has said three of his (Egbo) supporters were killed. Among those reportedly killed was Moses Anaughe, a former Commissioner, Federal Character Commission and aide to Omo-Agege. Also, former member of the Delta State House of Assembly, Chief Evans Ivwurie, was among those shot and reportedly battling for his life alongside other victims receiving medical attention. The latest bloodshed, which has triggered a fierce exchange of accusations between Omo-Agege’s camp and Olorogun Egbo, is the third major violent incident linked to political activities involving rival camps in the state. Clashes had erupted in the Warri-Effurun axis and Asaba, where one person was also killed. While Omo-Agege’s camp put the Uduere death toll at four, Egbo claimed three of his supporters were killed, with both sides accusing the other of instigating the violence. The recurrence of deadly confrontations, with the 2027 general elections still months away, has heightened concerns over the safety of political campaigns and the possibility of Delta becoming increasingly engulfed in political violence. item.title: Alleged assassination: We want IG to investigate, not Delta police — Omo-Agege
item.description: Former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, has called on the Inspector-General of Police to take over the investigation into the alleged assassination attempt on him in Delta State, saying he has no confidence in the state police command to deliver justice. Omo-Agege, the Nigeria Democratic Congress senatorial candidate for Delta Central, made the appeal on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, following an attack on his campaign entourage in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area. He alleged that police officers present during the incident failed to intervene as gunmen opened fire on his team, adding that the attack had heightened fears among opposition politicians in the state. “What we have learned is this: we are not safe here in Delta State. In fact, all members of the opposition party, NDC, most especially, we are all endangered,” he said. Omo-Agege claimed that six truckloads of policemen were deployed to the campaign venue but did not act when the shooting occurred. He accused the state police command of being unlikely to conduct an impartial investigation and urged the IGP to handle the case directly. “We do not expect any justice to come from the police here in Delta State. Neither do we expect any justice to come from the police on this very one,” he said. “We are appealing to the IG to take this matter over directly. We tried to reach him this evening. We couldn’t reach him.” The former lawmaker said he wanted the federal police leadership to investigate the incident, insisting that the state command should not be involved in the probe. He also called for justice for those affected by the attack, saying lives had been lost and several others were receiving treatment in hospitals. “We need justice. We need justice. We need justice for these four people who have been killed. We need justice for the 15 people who are critically injured and hospitalised right now,” Omo-Agege said. Despite the incident, he vowed not to abandon his campaign, dismissing suggestions that the attack could intimidate him into withdrawing from the race. “If the idea is that this is supposed to deter me from going forward with the campaigns, it’s a very big mistake and a big lie. Ain’t going to happen,” he said. He, however, appealed to his supporters to remain calm and avoid reprisals, warning that tensions remained high following the attack. item.title: Osun police bust child trafficking syndicate, rescue 16-day-old baby
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Osun State Police Command has dismantled a suspected child trafficking syndicate and rescued a 16-day-old baby boy allegedly sold for N1.5 million in a transaction involving two suspects. The command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed this in a statement on Monday, saying two suspects had been arrested in connection with the alleged trafficking. According to the police, the baby’s mother, Victoria Michael, 18, gave birth at a private hospital in Kajola on November 2 but was unable to cater for the child after the father, identified as Tayo, allegedly denied responsibility. Ojelabi said one of the mother’s friends, Comfort Olayinka, offered to help her find assistance through a contact in Abeokuta, Ogun State. He said Olayinka subsequently linked up with Oladipo Olamide, 46, who allegedly claimed to operate a non-governmental organisation providing care for less-privileged persons and offered to take the baby into its care. The police spokesman said the baby’s mother and Olayinka travelled to Abeokuta on November 5 and handed the child over to Olamide. However, Olayinka later allegedly told the mother that the baby had died and gave her a folded object resembling a baby, packed in a bag, which she was instructed to throw into Lafenwa River. Unknown to the mother, Olayinka had allegedly collected N450,000 from Olamide, purportedly for her upkeep. Ojelabi said police operatives, acting on intelligence, arrested Olamide in Abeokuta on November 17. During interrogation, the suspect allegedly confessed to selling the baby to one Mrs Bolanle Ruth for N1.5 million. He said Olamide subsequently led the operatives to Akure, Ondo State, where Ruth was arrested on November 18. According to the police, Ruth admitted paying N1.5 million for the baby and claimed she was promised that the necessary documents would be provided by an agency, but had yet to receive them. The police did not disclose the whereabouts or status of the other suspect, Olayinka, in the statement. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police in Osun State, Ibrahim Zungura, warned individuals and groups against child trafficking, assuring residents that the command would not tolerate the crime. He urged members of the public to provide useful information to security agencies to help prevent child trafficking and protect vulnerable children. item.title: Delta imposes curfew in Ughelli North after deadly violence
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Ughelli North Local Government Area following reports of deadly violence and gunshots in parts of the council. The curfew, which takes effect on Monday, November 23, 2026, will run daily from 6pm to 6am until further notice. The Secretary to the State Government, Dr Kingsley Emu, announced the restriction in a statement, saying the measure was aimed at restoring calm and bringing the security situation under control. According to the statement, the curfew covers the entire Ughelli North Local Government Area. The government urged residents to comply strictly with the directive. The development follows reports of deadly violence in the area, including an attack on the campaign team of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, during a campaign tour of Uduere. The attack reportedly left four persons dead and four others critically injured. The post Delta imposes curfew in Ughelli North after deadly violence appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Navy intercepts 89,000 litres of stolen crude, illegal diesel in Rivers
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has intercepted about 35,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and uncovered an illegal refining site containing an additional 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) in Rivers State. The operation, conducted on November 22 by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Pathfinder around Okarki Creek and Okarki Community in Ahoada West Local Government Area, followed credible intelligence. In a statement on Monday, the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, said the naval personnel intercepted a wooden boat conveying about 150 sacks containing suspected stolen crude oil. He said a subsequent operation in the adjoining area led to the discovery of an illegal refining site containing approximately 10 dugout pits, 180 sacks and a storage container holding an estimated 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined AGO. According to him, the combined volume of petroleum products recovered or identified during the operation was approximately 89,000 litres. “The boat, its contents and the refining site, including the stored products, were handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures,” the statement said. The Navy described the operation as part of its sustained campaign to disrupt the supply networks supporting crude oil theft and illegal refining activities in the Niger Delta. It said intercepting the suspected stolen crude oil and dismantling associated refining infrastructure would help deny oil thieves access to petroleum resources while addressing environmental degradation and revenue losses. The Service reaffirmed its commitment to intelligence-driven operations to protect critical oil and gas infrastructure, support national crude oil production and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. It added that operations would continue across the Niger Delta creeks to combat crude oil theft and illegal refining. item.title: Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32, AIG visits scene
item.description: …Urges enforcement of life jacket, passenger capacity regulations By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has visited Ayama-Ijaw waterside in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State following the boat mishap that claimed 32 lives. Udoette, who was accompanied by the Bayelsa State Commissioner of Police, Saka Ajao Adewale, visited the area on Monday to interact with marine transport workers and the Red Cross rescue team and receive updates on the ongoing search and recovery operation. During the visit, reports from the rescue site indicated that additional bodies had been recovered, raising the death toll from 29 to 32. The AIG commiserated with the Bayelsa State Government and residents over the tragedy, while commending President Bola Tinubu for his response and expression of sympathy following the incident. She expressed concern over alleged violations of maritime safety regulations, particularly the overloading of the vessel and failure to comply with life jacket requirements. According to her, the boat reportedly conveyed more than 500 passengers despite having a carrying capacity of 200. Udoette urged the state Ministry of Transport and marine unions to strengthen enforcement of safety regulations, particularly compulsory life jacket use and compliance with approved passenger limits. She also called for strict enforcement against operators who flout safety rules, stressing that passengers must take personal responsibility for their safety. Speaking with journalists, the AIG said she visited the waterside on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police to sympathise with the victims’ families and assess the situation. “I am here with my management team and the Bayelsa CP on behalf of the Inspector General of Police to sympathise with the people that died in the incident. I register our condolences and wish the injured quick recovery. “Besides, the maritime personnel told us of the refusal of passengers to obey safety rules, and the boat captain loaded over 500 persons for a boat with a 200-person capacity. That was a suicide mission and a disaster waiting to happen,” she said. Describing the deaths as avoidable, Udoette urged passengers and marine transport operators to comply with established safety regulations. “Some of these deaths are avoidable deaths. Many of the passengers refuse to obey safety rules. My Bible tells me obedience is better than sacrifice. There are rules and regulations on life jackets and overloading, but they refused. “For the living, this is a big lesson to everyone that wants to use a boat for their journey. They should listen to the rules. People should use common sense. This disaster is avoidable,” she added. She said the 2026 World AIDS Day theme, “Ending AIDS Starts with Access: Equity, Ownership and Sustainability,” highlighted the need for equitable access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care. “Access must not depend on where you live, what you earn or who you are. Ilori announced that NACA would unveil the National HIV Domestic Resource Mobilisation and Sustainability Strategy 2026–2030 on Dec. 1, as part of the World AIDS Day commemoration. According to her, the strategy will strengthen domestic financing, promote national ownership and sustain Nigeria’s HIV response amid declining global health funding. She also announced plans for a National Prevention Conference to explore innovative HIV prevention approaches, including self-testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and emerging prevention technologies. Dr Adebobola Bashorun, National Coordinator, National AIDS, Viral Hepatitis and STIs Control Programme (NASCP), said innovations would only save lives if they were accessible and affordable. “We can have the best technology and products, but without access they are useless,” he said. Bashorun said Nigeria was scaling up injectable HIV prevention medicines, oral PrEP and interventions to prevent mother-to-child transmission. item.title: Tinubu, Sanwo-Olu court Igbo community ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: …Urge national cohesion, economic inclusion By Olasunkanmi Akoni President Bola Tinubu and Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, have urged Nigerians to rise above ethnic and regional divisions, emphasising the need for national cohesion, mutual understanding and inclusive economic development. The leaders made the call on Monday at the Ndigbo Lagos State Town Hall, organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiative (NNDDI) at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Arts Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos. The engagement, attended by Igbo community leaders, business stakeholders and government officials, provided an opportunity to strengthen relations between the Igbo community and the Lagos and Federal Governments ahead of the 2027 general elections. Addressing participants, Tinubu urged Nigerians to embrace a shared national identity, irrespective of their ethnic, religious or regional backgrounds, saying the country’s development depended on the collective contributions of all citizens. He also stressed the importance of creating broad-based economic opportunities to enable Nigerians to contribute meaningfully to nation-building. “We must see ourselves as one people with a shared future. “Nigeria must rise above its divisions, because our true development depends on the active participation and commitment of every single citizen, regardless of background,” the President said. Earlier, Sanwo-Olu commended Tinubu for attending the gathering, describing his presence as an affirmation of the important role played by the Igbo community in the socioeconomic development of Lagos State. He acknowledged the contributions of Igbo political leaders, entrepreneurs, business associates and other stakeholders to the growth of the state. “The President’s presence here today is a significant gesture of recognition for Ndigbo and their rightful place in Lagos. “We deeply value the enduring contributions and longstanding partnerships of the political leaders, business associates, and stakeholders who continue to build this state alongside us,” the governor said. Reflecting on Nigeria’s democratic journey, particularly the political developments of 1999, 2003 and 2007, Sanwo-Olu also paid tribute to past and present leaders whose contributions helped shape the country’s political evolution. The town hall was designed to deepen engagement, address concerns affecting the Igbo community in Lagos and strengthen collaboration between community representatives and the two tiers of government. item.title: Obi Meets Niger State Residents, Urges Nigerians To Turn Out For 2027 Elections
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the 2027 general elections and remain at their polling units until their votes are counted and transmitted. Obi made the call during a campaign visit to Suleja, Niger State, where he urged voters to resist attempts to manipulate the outcome of the elections by ensuring that their votes were properly accounted for. He also criticised President Bola Tinubu, claiming that the president lacked the physical strength required to govern the country and was more interested in retaining power for personal gains than serving Nigerians. Obi, who is seeking the presidency for the second time, also promised to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, pledging that his administration would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected. Niger residents gather for an engagement of NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X He said Niger State would play a role in achieving the target, citing the state’s resources as part of the potential support for his proposed power-sector plan. The former Anambra State governor has been holding town hall meetings and engaging residents in different states ahead of the 2027 general elections. NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X Obi contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party, finishing third with 6,101,533 votes, behind Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who polled 8,794,726 votes, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, who received 6,984,520 votes. Tinubu is seeking re-election in 2027, while Obi is contesting under the NDC. Ahead of the election, major contenders include Tinubu under the APC, Atiku of the ADC, and Obi of the NDC. Other parties include the AAC, PDP, APM, SDP, PRP, Labour Party, and YPP. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are slated for February 6, 2027. item.title: APC’ll win three South-East states; Obi will take Abia, Anambra — Bwala
item.description: The Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has projected that the All Progressives Congress will win three states in the South-East in the 2027 general elections, while conceding that Peter Obi could retain a stronghold in Abia and Anambra. Bwala made the projection during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief on Monday, where he was asked how the ruling party intended to secure victories in the region. He said Obi’s popularity in the two states could make them difficult for the APC to win, but expressed confidence that the party would prevail in the remaining South-East states. “We will struggle in Abia. You see, in Abia and Anambra, Peter has a very convincing presence. Even in these two states, I am assuming that if we lose, we still come second, which is not a bad thing. Apart from these two states, the remainder of the states, we are winning,” Bwala said. The presidential aide, however, stressed that his assessment was a projection rather than a definitive prediction, noting that different political actors could arrive at varying conclusions from available data. He said the party was willing to acknowledge areas where it might face difficulties rather than make sweeping claims about its chances. “Where we think we may not, and I use the word advisedly because none of what I’m saying is cast in stone, right? It is projection, and two people from the same political party can have different projections based on our own interpretation of data,” he said. Bwala added that admitting potential weaknesses was more honest than claiming the APC would win everywhere, noting that his use of the word “struggle” referred specifically to the party’s chances of winning those states. The presidential adviser also expressed confidence in the APC’s overall prospects ahead of the 2027 elections, dismissing the opposition’s preparedness to challenge the ruling party. “I do not think the opposition is ready. Those who understand the political trajectory can see that they are already facing defeat,” he said. item.title: FG seeks 18-month completion period for new Carter Bridge
item.description: The Federal Government is seeking reduction in the period for construction of the new Carter Bridge. The Minister of Works, Sen. Dave Umahi, told the contractor handling the project, China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC), to look at the possibility of reducing the time frame from 36 months to 18 months or 24 months. He said that the aim was to save more money and ensure that the new Carter Bridge would come on board before the existing one would go down. He said that CCECC had completed five per cent of the 1.9km bridge project without being paid any mobilisation fee. “No mobilisation fee has been paid to them, and the duration of this project is 36 months but I am striking a deal with their management, having seen that they have gone up to five per cent. “We are going to release, within this week, 30 per cent mobilisation fee to CCECC. “Another deal will probably be if we can reduce the construction period to about 18 months to 24 months; then, they can apply for loan so they can set up two other sections of piling. ” if they will do that, we are ready to give them a loan of 20 per cent so that they can set up, but they must give us APG – Advance Payment Guarantee,” the minister said. According to him, the Federal Government already has the APG for the 30 per cent mobilisation fee. “We are not allowed to pay more than 30 per cent but we can give a loan based on an agreement.” He emphasised that the bridge’s piling must be on a minimum of Schedule 60 thick steel pile. He said that the CCECC was meeting the specification. “We are very happy about that. We also directed that when they start their piling, we have to do a number of big lumps to protect the piles at the seabed,” Umahi said The post FG seeks 18-month completion period for new Carter Bridge appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Holding election with disputed voters’ register amounts to rigging – APM
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Allied People’s Movement (APM) has warned that conducting the 2027 general elections with a disputed voters’ register would amount to rigging, accusing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of creating room for electoral manipulation by postponing its clean-up until after the polls. The party said the decision could undermine confidence in the electoral process, warning that unresolved concerns over the register could compromise the credibility of the 2027 elections. Responding to Vanguard’s enquiry on INEC’s decision, APM National Publicity Secretary, Abubakar Yusuf, described the postponement as another form of electoral manipulation and vowed that the party would resist any attempt to subvert the will of voters. “That’s another form of rigging the 2027 elections. Going into an election with a controversial register is tantamount to rigging, just like we had the case of electronic voting and BVAS,” Yusuf said. Citing the Kogi Central senatorial district election, Yusuf alleged that the experience showed how electoral outcomes could be manipulated in favour of the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. “You remember in Kogi Central, election results were written by APC and the candidate declared as governor. I think that’s what they are going to adopt this time around,” he alleged. He insisted that APM would not accept any attempt to compromise the electoral process, declaring that the party would join other opposition groups to resist interference with voters’ choices. “APM will not succumb to INEC gimmicks. Any attempt to rig or tamper with the judgement of Nigerians in the forthcoming general elections will be resisted by not only APM, but opposition parties,” he said. Yusuf urged INEC to put its electoral preparations in order, warning against any action capable of compromising the 2027 elections. “INEC must do the needful by putting everything in order,” he added. item.title: Ghana defeat Morocco to win maiden Amputee Football World Cup title
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, have emerged champions of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup after defeating Morocco 1-0 in the final held in Mexico. The victory marks Ghana’s first title in the competition and a historic achievement for the country’s football. The decisive goal came from a free-kick by Mubarik Mohammed, whose effort led to an own goal by Morocco, giving the Black Challenge the advantage they held until the final whistle. Mohammed also finished the tournament as its highest goalscorer, finding the net seven times during Ghana’s impressive campaign. The Black Challenge had earlier secured their place in the final after defeating defending champions Turkey on penalties in the semi-finals. They also recorded a 2-0 victory over Egypt to book their place in the last four. The triumph over Morocco brings Ghana’s successful campaign to a fitting end and earns the team its first world title in amputee football. item.title: [PHOTOS] FG Targets December For Reopening Of Eko, Iddo Bridges
item.description: The Federal Government has assured Lagos residents that the Eko and Iddo bridges will be fully functional by December 2026, as rehabilitation and reconstruction works continue on the two critical transport links. The Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, gave the assurance during an inspection of the ongoing projects in Lagos, where he assessed the progress of work and commended the quality of interventions being carried out. This image shows ongoing reconstruction of the Iddo Bridge in Lagos. (Photo: Temitope Abe/Channels TV) At Eko Bridge, rehabilitation works were focused on addressing concerns surrounding some of its supporting structural components, while Iddo Bridge is undergoing reconstruction. Umahi expressed satisfaction with the progress recorded at both sites, assuring that the contractors would deliver the projects within the December deadline. “We are satisfied with what they’re doing. They are very fast in what they’re doing. They have good knowledge of what they are doing. And so we — as Ministry of Works — we are very satisfied,” the minister said. “And they promised us that by December, they will definitely complete the job and the full integrity of the bridge will be restored.” This image shows ongoing reconstruction of the Iddo Bridge in Lagos. (Photo: Temitope Abe/Channels TV) The inspection forms part of the Federal Government’s efforts to restore the two important infrastructure links, which serve thousands of commuters and businesses across Lagos. The ongoing construction activities have continued to affect movement around the affected corridors, with motorists and commuters having to contend with traffic disruptions. Umahi (2nd-left) commended the level of work done on the projects so far. (Photo: Temitope Abe/Channels TV) The minister’s assurance comes amid expectations that completing the projects will improve connectivity, ease traffic congestion, and enhance the safety of road users. Attention will now be on the contractors’ ability to meet the December deadline while ensuring that the restored infrastructure meets the required structural and safety standards.
